messages.text: quick sanity check. our payments API at Ledgerline (Go + Postgres) is getting retry storms from a partner bank and we're seeing duplicate transfers. I'm the backend eng who owns the transfers service so this one's on me. is an idempotency key table enough or do i need advisory locks too

An idempotency key table is usually enough if you insert the key and the transfer in the same transaction and put a unique constraint on the key. A duplicate request then fails on the constraint and you return the stored response instead of creating a second transfer. Advisory locks only help if you make slow external calls before writing anything.
ok makes sense. we do call the ledger provider before the insert tho

Then reserve the key first: insert it with a 'pending' status, commit, call the provider, and update the row with the result. A retry that finds a pending row can wait briefly or return 409. That stops two workers from calling the provider for the same key.
perfect. totally unrelated — I'm organising a Ramadan food drive for Masjid Al-Noor in Bay Ridge this year, aiming for 300 grocery boxes. any quick tips for tracking pledges?

A shared spreadsheet with columns for donor, item, quantity and drop-off date works well. You could also set up a Google Form so pledges land in the sheet automatically. Posting a running total in your group chat helps keep momentum.
nah the aunties will never fill a form lol. we'll keep it in the whatsapp group and I'll tally by hand

messages.text: whats the actual difference between context.WithTimeout and context.WithDeadline in Go

They do the same thing. WithTimeout(ctx, d) is just WithDeadline(ctx, time.Now().Add(d)). Use WithTimeout when you think in durations ('give this call 2 seconds') and WithDeadline when you already have an absolute time, like a request deadline passed down from upstream.

messages.text: I need to build an interview scorecard for an ops coordinator. small studio, 6 people, nobody has ever been 'hired' properly before. can you give me 5 competencies?

Here are five that suit a first ops hire: 1) organisation and follow-through, 2) written communication, 3) comfort with ambiguity, 4) basic finance/admin literacy (invoices, expenses), 5) judgement about what to escalate. Score each 1-4 with a short behavioural anchor so interviewers agree on what a 3 looks like.
good. what would a 3 look like for 'comfort with ambiguity'

A 3 might be: 'Gives an example of a task with unclear ownership, made a sensible first move without waiting, and checked in at the right moment.' A 4 would add that they set up something lasting, like a process or a doc, so the ambiguity didn't come back.
love it. ok next: right to work checks. we've literally never done one

In the UK you must check right to work before the start date. For British or Irish passport holders you can check the original document in person or use a certified digital identity provider. For people with immigration status you use the Home Office online check with their share code. Keep a dated copy of the check on file.
ok so one of the two candidates would need sponsoring, Amara Iyer, and we don't have a sponsor licence. is getting one quick?

Usually not. A sponsor licence application commonly takes around eight weeks to decide, plus time to prepare documents and pay the fee, and you need someone in the business to act as the authorising officer. For a first hire with an end-of-April offer target it's unlikely to be ready in time.
yeah thought so.
That's fair to her. You could still interview her and keep her in mind for a later role once the studio is bigger, if she's strong.
maybe. ok, onboarding checklist for day 1? keep it short, I'm off to Lisbon for my sister's hen do 18–22 April so I want this done before

Day 1: laptop and accounts ready, welcome from the founder, walk through the studio's tools, a short 'how we work' doc, lunch with the team, and one small real task they can finish by end of day. Week 1: meet each person one-to-one and agree 30/60/90-day goals.
the 'one small real task' thing is good. what about probation, 3 or 6 months

Three months is common for operational roles and gives you a reasonably quick read; six months suits roles where results take longer to show. Whichever you pick, put a mid-point review in the diary so there are no surprises.
3 months it is, with a review at 6 weeks. thanks, this saved me an afternoon
Glad it helped. Good luck with the interviews, and enjoy Lisbon.

messages.text: on call and payments-gateway pods keep getting OOMKilled. limits are 512Mi, it's a JVM service. where do i start

Start by checking whether the JVM heap is sized relative to the container limit. On recent JDKs, set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage (for example 70-75) instead of a fixed -Xmx, so the heap leaves room for metaspace, threads and off-heap buffers. Then compare `kubectl top pod` against the limit and look at the pod's last termination reason.
MaxRAMPercentage isn't set at all lol. Xmx is hardcoded to 512m

That's very likely the cause: with -Xmx equal to the container limit, any non-heap memory pushes the process over 512Mi and the kernel kills it. Either drop -Xmx to around 360m or switch to MaxRAMPercentage=70, and consider raising the limit to 768Mi if traffic is growing.
ok pushing MaxRAMPercentage=70 + limit 768Mi. while it rolls out, unrelated q: can a landlord in Kenya keep a deposit for 'repainting'? mine is refusing to give back my KES 90,000

I can't give legal advice, but generally a deposit is meant to cover unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, and routine repainting after a normal tenancy is often treated as wear and tear. Check what your lease says about deductions and whether you have move-in and move-out photos. A written demand letter is a common first step.
yeah the lease says 'damage beyond fair wear'. I moved out on 31 Jan and just moved to Kilimani, so I have all the photos from both ends
Good, that helps. Photos plus the lease clause make a clear demand letter: list the deposit amount, the move-out date, the condition evidence, and a deadline for repayment, for example 14 days.
his name is Haris Lodhi, I'll send him the letter on friday. I'm devops, not a lawyer lol
Fair enough. Keep the tone factual and attach the photos. Meanwhile, how's the rollout looking?
2 of 12 pods restarted with the new settings. memory sitting at ~540Mi, under the 768 limit
That's a healthy margin. Watch it through the next traffic peak; if it climbs steadily rather than levelling off, you may have a leak, and a heap dump would be the next step.
should I also add a VPA or is that overkill

For one service it's probably overkill right now. A VPA in recommendation-only mode can be useful to see what it would suggest without letting it change anything, which is a low-risk way to tune limits later.
nah not tonight. maybe I'll take the landlord thing to the Rent Restriction Tribunal, idk yet
That's an option some tenants use if a demand letter doesn't work. It's worth seeing how he responds first.
all 12 pods green. going to sleep before something else pages me
Nice work. Good night, and good luck with the letter.

[2] assistant: Start with the payoff instead of the greeting. Something like: 'One of these mics costs ten times more than the other, and I bet you can't tell which. Let's find out.' You can introduce yourself and the channel after the first reveal. Want a couple more options in different tones?
[3] user: yeah give me a funny one and a serious one
[4] assistant: Funny: 'I spent £300 on a microphone so you don't have to, and honestly my cat sounds the same on both.' Serious: 'Does expensive audio gear actually make you sound better, or are we paying for the box? I ran a blind test to find out.' Both lead into the same reveal, so you can pick whichever matches your usual tone.
[5] user: funny one is good. now thumbnail text, 3 words max, has to read on a phone screen
[6] assistant: A few options: 'CAN YOU HEAR IT?', '£30 vs £300', or 'WHICH IS WHICH?'. Keep the text in a heavy sans-serif with a thick outline, and put it on the opposite side from the two mics so faces and gear stay visible. High-contrast yellow on a dark background tends to survive tiny previews well.
[7] user: £30 vs £300 it is. ok boring stuff, i upload every thursday at 6pm so can you write the description with timestamp chapters? just use placeholders for the times

I recorded the same script on both and tested it blind. 00:00 Intro, 00:00 The setup, 00:00 Round one: voiceover, 00:00 Round two: noisy room, 00:00 The reveal, 00:00 Verdict.' Add your gear links under the chapters, and put the most important sentence in the first two lines because that's all that shows before 'show more'.
[9] user: thanks. sorry im scattered, my SBR exam is sometime in june and after missing the pass mark by 3 marks last time i cant afford to lose a week to a video lol
[10] assistant: That's a lot to carry, and missing by three marks is frustrating but also a sign you're close. For the channel, try batching: record two videos in one session, then edit them in the gaps. That way the exam prep doesn't get squeezed by a rolling weekly deadline.
[11] user: good idea. Isla Hayes and I do timed mock papers every sunday, that's my fixed study block
[12] assistant: A fixed weekly block with a partner is a solid setup, because timed papers train exactly what the exam rewards. Between mocks, short targeted sessions on weak topics usually beat long re-reading. After each paper, spend as long reviewing your answers as you spent writing them.
[13] user: should i switch to resolve for the edits? my current editor keeps crashing on long timelines
[14] assistant: It depends on your timing. Resolve's free version is capable and handles long timelines well, but the learning curve costs a few weeks of slower work. If you're under pressure right now, you could finish the current project where it is and trial Resolve on something small afterwards. Also try clearing the cache and using proxies, which fixes many crashes.

[16] assistant: A few: 'Blind Spot', 'Ear Test', 'Sound Check', or 'Gear Gauntlet'. 'Blind Spot' works nicely because the tests are blind and it hints at things people miss. Keep the title card short so it doesn't eat into your hook.

messages.text: can you explain the IFRS 15 five step model simply? i keep mixing up performance obligations and the transaction price

Think of it as five questions. 1) Is there a contract? 2) What are the separate promises (performance obligations)? 3) What is the total price you expect to receive (transaction price)? 4) How is that price split across the promises? 5) When is each promise delivered, which is when you recognise revenue. Performance obligations are the 'what', and the transaction price is the 'how much'.

Ha, noted, though I think you'll be fine. Step 3 question: a company sells a bundle for £1,000 with a possible £100 discount if the customer pays within 10 days, and it expects the customer to take the discount. What is the transaction price, and why?

However, charging a small fee can help them maintain collections, so I partly disagree that entry should always be free.'

Good start. Your position is clear, and 'partly disagree' is a legitimate IELTS stance. Fix 'becuase' to 'because', and consider replacing 'important' with something more specific, like 'vital for preserving collective memory'. Next, add a concrete example in the following sentence, such as a national museum that charges only foreign visitors.
ha typo, i type too fast. what linking words do people overuse btw

'Moreover', 'furthermore' and 'in addition' show up in nearly every band 6 essay. Examiners prefer linking that follows the logic of your argument: 'as a result', 'by contrast', 'that said'. Use each sparingly and vary them.
ok noted. totally unrelated, i'm choosing fonts for a restaurant menu, thinking Playfair Display for headings and something clean for body. too cliche?

Playfair is popular but not tired if your layout is confident. For body text try Work Sans, Lato or Source Sans, all very legible at small sizes. Keep the weight contrast strong and limit yourself to two families.
will test both. random q, how much is 45,000 KES in USD roughly?
At roughly 129 shillings to the dollar, 45,000 KES is about 350 USD. Rates move daily, so check a live converter before quoting or paying anything.
thx. ok back to the essay, i only get 40 mins for task 2 in the real test right? my exam is 25 April so i need to get timing sorted

Yes, roughly 40 minutes is the recommended time for task 2, and it carries more weight than task 1. A workable split is 5 minutes planning, 30 writing and 5 checking. Practise with a timer on your phone and stop when it rings.
got it. i need 7 overall for the Leeds MA so there's no room for panic. can you also help me write a polite thank-you note to a teacher?

Of course. Here is a short version: 'Dear [Name], thank you for the generous feedback and the extra practice papers. It has made a real difference to my confidence, and I am very grateful.' Add one specific detail about what helped most to make it feel personal.
